predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: the small territory around Söğüt in Bithynia that Osman I held 'by 1300'

successors.name: Republic of Turkey
successors.text: Anatolia and Eastern Thrace, the last Ottoman shape, with the Smyrna enclave retaken on 9 September 1922

successors.name: Kingdom of Hejaz
successors.text: the Hejaz, proclaimed independent in the Arab Revolt of 1916

successors.name: French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon
successors.text: Syria and Lebanon, occupied in 1918 and mandated to France in 1920

successors.name: Kingdom of Iraq
successors.text: Iraq (the Ottoman vilayets of Baghdad and Basra, and Mosul from 1926)

ledger.x: c. 1299: Osman I founds the Ottoman principality at Söğüt in Bithynia. The page calls the date 1299 'purely symbolic' (By 1300 Osman rules 'a small territory around the town of Söğüt'); the main article's infobox gives 'c. 1299'. No page names an overlord; the land is Byzantine Bithynia, where the Battle of Bapheus…
1326: Orhan conquers Bursa.
1331: Nicaea (İznik) is Orhan's capital from 1331 on the infobox.
1331: the capital moves from Söğüt to Nicaea (İznik).
1335: the capital moves to Prousa (Bursa).
1345-6: Orhan annexes the Karesi beylik.
1354: the Ottomans gain Çimpe Castle on the Gallipoli peninsula, their first foothold in Europe.
1362-3: Murad I takes Adrianople.
1363: the capital moves to Edirne (Adrianople), 'his new capital in 1363.'
1363: Cliopatria's shape adds about 73 cells around Ankara and Eskişehir in 1363, the year its Ahi Republic row ends (1362).
By 1370: Murad controls most of Thrace.
1371: John V accepts vassalage.
26 September 1371: after the Battle of Maritsa 'Macedonia and parts of Greece fell under Ottoman power.'
By 1376: Tsar Shishman of Bulgaria 'accepted vassal status under Murad.'
1385: Murad I takes Sofia.
1386: Murad takes Niš.
1387: Thessaloniki falls to the Ottomans.
1390: Stefan Lazarević becomes Bayezid's vassal.
After early 1393: Tarnovo is stormed and Shishman executed, ending the Bulgarian vassalage.
1393: Bayezid annexes the Tarnovo tsardom.
c. 1394-5: Bayezid annexes Thessaly, and the Duchy of Athens accepts Ottoman overlordship.
ledger.cp: Greek lords of Thessaly (the page names none)

ledger.x: 1395: Mircea of Wallachia accepts vassalage after Rovine ('Bayezid's forces were defeated at Rovine, and Mircea of Wallachia accepted vassalage').
After 1395: 'Dobrudzha was annexed at some point after this.'

Late 14th century: 'Towards the end of the 14th century, the Ottomans advanced further into Anatolia' by acquiring towns or through marriage alliances, and 'by the close of the century, the early Ottoman leaders had conquered large parts of land from Karamanids'.
ledger.cp: Anatolian beyliks of the Sivas region (no page opened names them)

ledger.x: 1396: Vidin is annexed after Nicopolis, and 'Bulgaria ceased to exist.'
1402: Timur defeats Bayezid at Ankara and the beyliks regain their lands: 'their territories were restored to them after the Ottoman defeat suffered against Tamerlane in 1402.'
ledger.cp: Anatolian beyliks restored by Timur (Karaman, Germiyan, Aydın and others)

ledger.x: c. 1402-1410 (exact date not given): Suleyman holds Edirne and returns Thessaloniki to Byzantium.
1402: 'Thessaloniki, Macedonia, and Kosovo' are lost after Ankara and recovered 'in the 1430s-1450s under Murad II' (main article).
ledger.cp: Balkan successor lords (the page names none)

ledger.x: About 1402 (bridging): Wallachia's vassalage lapses.
1412: Mehmed invades the Balkans.

c. 1415: Mehmed I and Murad II 'reincorporated most of these beyliks into Ottoman territory in a period of about 25 years.' Cliopatria's shape adds İzmir and Manisa in 1415, the year its Saruhan row ends (1414).
c. 1415: part of the reincorporation of the beyliks 'in a period of about 25 years'; Cliopatria's Menteshe row ends 1414 and its Ottoman shape adds Muğla in 1415.
1419: Mehmed I restores Wallachia's vassalage.
1422: 'Most of Albania was conquered' after 1396 (undated); Cliopatria's shape adds about 62 Albanian cells in 1422.
1429: the reincorporation of the beyliks 'in a period of about 25 years' under Mehmed I and Murad II; Cliopatria's shape adds about 327 cells in 1429, the year after its Teke row ends (1428).
1429: part of the same reincorporation; the Anatolian beyliks page's table gives Germiyan as 1300-1429, which the page's tables give as when each state existed, not when the Ottomans took it.
1430: Murad II takes Thessaloniki.
1430s: Macedonia is recovered.
ledger.cp: Balkan successor lords (the page names none)

ledger.x: 1431: Cliopatria's shape adds about 46 cells in Greece and Albania in 1431, which is where its Despotate of Epirus row (1206-1481) sits.
1443: 'Niš and Sofia fell to the Christians in 1443' in Hunyadi's campaign.
1448: 'Another peace treaty was signed in 1448,' giving the Ottomans Wallachia, Bulgaria and part of Albania, after Hunyadi's second campaign at Kosovo.
29 May 1453: Mehmed II takes Constantinople.
29 May 1453: the Byzantine vassal state ends with the fall of Constantinople; Mehmed II had annulled all treaties with Byzantium in 1451.
29 May 1453: Constantinople becomes the capital (infobox 'Constantinople (Istanbul): 1453-1922').
1458: the Ottomans take the Duchy of Athens.
August 1458: Mehmed II annexes the north of the Morea.
1459: Cliopatria's shape grows by about 301 cells in 1459 (Serbia 173, Greece 43, Kosovo 39, Montenegro 23, Albania 18).
1459: the Serbian vassalage of 1390 ends as the land enters the Cliopatria shape.
29 May 1460: Mehmed II takes Mystras and the Despotate of the Morea ends.
1461: the Trebizond eyalet is created on the 'Southeast Black Sea coast' (table: 1461, Trebizond).
1462: the Eyalet page has no entry for the Isfendiyar lands.
1463: the Eyalet page lists the Bosnia eyalet from 1580 ('Bosnia, border with the Habsburgs'); Cliopatria's shape adds about 137 Bosnian cells in 1463 and 70 in Greece.
1468: Karaman becomes an Ottoman eyalet seated at Konya (table: Karaman, '1468 (text); 1483 (table)').
1475: the Eyalet page lists 'Kefe (Theodosia)' as the Crimea eyalet from 1568; Cliopatria's shape adds Kefe, Kerch and Azov in 1475.
1475: the khan of Crimea is an Ottoman vassal; the main article has 'the Crimean khan, under Ottoman command, burns Moscow' in 1571.
1482: Cliopatria's shape adds about 26 cells in Herzegovina and 5 in Montenegro in 1482, the year after its Bosnia row ends (1481).
1487: Cliopatria's shape adds about 47 cells in Ukraine and 20 in Moldova in 1487, which is the Budjak coast of Moldavia.
1515: Selim I 'conquered territories of the Beylik of Ramadan and the Beylik of Dulkadir in 1515,' during his campaign against the Mamluk Sultanate.
1515: the Ramadan beylik's territories are conquered by Selim I in the same campaign ('conquered territories of the Beylik of Ramadan and the Beylik of Dulkadir in 1515').
1516: 'The Ottomans first captured Diyarbekir in southeastern Anatolia' when the Mamluk war began.
24 August 1516: Selim I wins Syria at Marj Dabiq.
28 October 1516: the Mamluks lose Palestine at Yaunis Khan near Gaza ('another Mamluk defeat').
1517 (doubtful): the Eyalet page's table, as extracted, lists a Yemen eyalet created 1517 together with Egypt, Algiers and Syria; it was lost in 1636 and re-established in 1849.
24 January 1517: the Ottomans win at Ridaniya and take Cairo.
December 1517: the Hejaz becomes Ottoman.
1521: Suleiman takes Belgrade.
1526: Mohács opens the Ottoman-Habsburg contest for Hungary.
1526: southern Hungary and Syrmia pass to the Ottomans after Mohács (main article: 'Victory at Mohács; Ottoman rule is established in present-day Hungary and other Central European lands').
After 1526 'intermittently': Transylvania, Wallachia and Moldavia 'become tributary principalities.'
After 1526 'intermittently': Moldavia becomes a tributary principality (main article).
1529: Cliopatria's 1529 shape adds 43 cells in Hungary, 16 in Croatia and 25 in Austria.
1533: the Iranian campaign of 1533-6 opens the contest for Iraq.
1535: Suleiman takes Baghdad.
1540: Venice sues for terms.
1541: the Turks seize Buda.
1547: 'Ferdinand officially recognises Ottoman ascendancy in Hungary.'
1551: the Tripolitania eyalet is created (table: 1551, 'Tripolitania (Tripoli in the West)').
ledger.cp: Knights of St John (Tripoli; no dossier)

ledger.x: 1552: the Temeşvar eyalet is created over the Banat (table: 1552, Temeşvar, 'Banat region'); the Banat is lost for good in 1718.
1555: the Peace of Amasya ends the first Ottoman-Safavid war: it 'partitions the Caucasus; Western Armenia, western Kurdistan, and Western Georgia go to the Ottomans.'
1555: the Peace of Amasya gives the Ottomans 'Western Armenia, western Kurdistan, and Western Georgia.'
1555: 'Western Georgia' passes to the Ottomans under the Peace of Amasya.
1556: the Eyalet page lists the Algiers eyalet from 1517 to 1830, but Cliopatria draws Algeria in the Ottoman shape only for 1519-1520 and from 1556.
1557: Massawa is taken and Habesh Eyalet set up.
1560: the Al-Hasa eyalet is created ('Eastern Arabia', 1560, lost 1670).
ledger.cp: Bani Khalid and the Gulf coast (page names none)

ledger.x: 22 July 1570: the Ottomans besiege Nicosia, opening the Cyprus War.
August 1571: Famagusta falls and the contest for Cyprus ends.
August 1571: Cyprus becomes Ottoman.
1574: the final Ottoman conquest of Tunis.
1578: the Ottoman-Safavid war of 1578-1590 opens in the Caucasus.
1578-9: Georgia and Shirvan pass to the Ottomans.
1585: the Tabriz eyalet is created (Eyalet page: 'Tabriz (1585–1603)').
1587: Hamadan and Luristan fall to the Ottomans.
1590: the Treaty of Constantinople ends the 1578-1590 war.
1593: the Long Turkish War against Habsburg Austria begins ('1593-1606: Long Turkish War').
1596: Eger falls to the Ottomans ('Eger fell to the Ottomans in 1596'); the Eyalet page creates the Eger eyalet in 1596 and Kanije in 1600 'from a border fortress that fell in 1600.'
1600: the border fortress of Kanije falls and becomes an eyalet (table: 1600, Kanije, 'Hungary, from a border fortress that fell in 1600').
1603: the Ottoman-Safavid war of 1603-1612 (1603-1618 on the main article) opens; Shah Abbas takes back Tabriz.
1603: the Safavids take Tbilisi.

21 October 1603: the Safavids capture Tabriz ('The Safavid army was able to capture Tabriz on 21 October 1603'); Nakhchivan follows the same month ('The Safavids entered Nakhchivan at the same month soon after the city was evacuated by the Ottomans').
June 1604: the Safavids capture Yerevan.
1606: 'The Long War ended with the Treaty of Zsitvatorok in 1606' and 'did not yield significant territorial changes.'
June 1606: 'Abbas I was able to liberate Ganja, Baku, Shirvan, and Shamakhi in Azerbaijan in June 1606' (Ottoman-Safavid War 1603-1618).
1612: Cliopatria drops about 147 Georgian cells west of Kartli from its Ottoman shape in 1612 and does not restore them until 1727.

20 November 1612: 'The Treaty of Nasuh Pasha was signed on 20 November 1612' (Ottoman-Safavid War 1603-1618); its infobox lists Daghestan among the territories the Safavids regain ('Azerbaijan, Georgia, Erivan Province, Daghestan, Shirvan, Karabakh, Lorestan, Khuzestan').

20 November 1612: the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha ends the first phase of the war of 1603-1618 ('The Treaty of Nasuh Pasha was signed on 20 November 1612'; it 'secured the 1555 borders envisaged by the Peace of Amasya'); the page's war runs to 1618 (a later war of 1616-1618 ends with the Treaty of Serav, also a Persian…
14 January 1624: Shah Abbas takes Baghdad.
14 January 1624: Baghdad is lost to Persia.
1624-1625: the Persians hold most of Iraq.
1636: the Yemen eyalet is lost (table: Yemen 1517, ended '1636; re-established 1849, lost 1872').
December 1638: Murad IV retakes Baghdad.
17 May 1639: the Treaty of Zuhab ends the war.
1645: the Cretan War (1645-1669) begins; the Ottomans 'captured Crete'.
1663: the Ottomans 'conquered the fortress of Nové Zámky' (Uyvar); the war ended at the Battle of St.
1669: 'Conquest of Crete is completed.'
1669: Crete becomes Ottoman (the Eyalet page creates the Crete (Girid) eyalet in 1669).
1672-1676: the Ottomans expand 'into Polish southern Ukraine'; the Podolia eyalet, with Khotyn and Kamianets-Podilskyi, is 'formed in 1676' on the main article and created 1672 on the Eyalet page.
1677: Cliopatria drops about 213 cells in Ukraine.
1683: the Second Siege of Vienna fails, opening the Great Turkish War ('1683: Second Siege of Vienna fails'); the area reaches 5.2 M km2 on the infobox.
1684: the Morean War (1684-1699) begins: Venice captured 'the Morea, Lefkada, Aigina, and parts of Dalmatia.'
1685: the Uyvar eyalet (1663-1685) ends in the Great Turkish War.
1686: the Holy League 'reconquered Buda.'
1687: the Morea passes to Venice during the Morean War (1684-1699); the Eyalet page ends the Morea eyalet in 1687.
1691: Cliopatria drops 36 cells in Hungary, 32 in Romania and 18 in Serbia.
July 1696: Peter I takes Azov.

26 January 1699: the Treaty of Karlowitz ends the Great Turkish War: 'secured territories, the rest of Hungary and overlordship of Transylvania for the Austrians'; the Ottomans 'surrender significant territory.'
26 January 1699: Hungary, Slavonia and Transylvania pass to the Austrians at Karlowitz.
26 January 1699: Karlowitz gives 'overlordship of Transylvania' to the Austrians, ending Ottoman suzerainty.
1699: Podolia returns to Poland.
1699: the Morean War ends with the Morea in Venetian hands: the war brought 'the end of Ottoman dominance in the eastern Mediterranean Sea.'
July 1705: Husayn bin Ali's coup founds the Husainid beylik, 'formally part of the Ottoman Empire'; the beys 'remained faithful to the Sublime Porte, but reigned as monarchs'.
1706: Algeria leaves the Ottoman shape and Cliopatria starts its Regency of Algiers row.
1711: Ahmed Karamanli 'murdered the Ottoman governor of Tripolitania and seized the throne in the 1711 Karamanli coup'; Tripolitania 'continued to pay nominal tribute to the Ottoman padishah'.
1711-1713: Azov returns after the Pruth campaign.
1714: the Seventh Ottoman-Venetian War (1714-1718) begins; the Ottomans 'recaptured the Morea, Tinos, and Aigina,' the last Venetian holdings in the Aegean.
1715: the Morea eyalet is re-established (table: 1620, Morea, '1687; re-established 1715, lost 1829').
1716: the Temeşvar eyalet (1552-1716) ends; Prince Eugene 'defeated the Ottomans at Petrovaradin in 1716.'
1716: Prince Eugene beats the Ottomans at Petrovaradin and takes Belgrade in 1717 (war of 1716-1718).
1718: the Treaty of Passarowitz ends the Austro-Turkish War of 1716-1718.
1718: 'The treaty gave the Austrians the Banat of Temeswar, Serbia, and Oltenia' (Passarowitz).
1718: the Seventh Ottoman-Venetian War ends with the Morea, Tinos and Aigina Ottoman and 'the last Venetian holdings in the Aegean' gone.
1727: Cliopatria adds about 1,213 cells (Iran 890, Azerbaijan 217, Armenia 82, Georgia 13).
1730: the Ottoman-Persian war of 1730-1735 begins (a 'Persian victory', Treaty of Constantinople 1736).
1736: the Treaty of Constantinople ends the war of 1730-1735, a Persian victory.
1736: Persia recovers its lands ('Persian victory', 1730-1735, Treaty of Constantinople 1736).
1737: the Austro-Russian-Turkish War is dated 1735-1739 on the main article; the Habsburg wars page dates its end, not its start.
1739: the Treaty of Belgrade ends the war.
1739: the Habsburgs 'ceded to the Ottomans Serbia (including Belgrade), the southern Banat of Temeswar, and northern Bosnia'; 'The Sava and Danube became the demarcation line' (Treaty of Belgrade).
1739: 'Ottomans cede the demilitarized Azov to Russia, as well as the Zaporozhye region'.
1768: the Russo-Turkish War of 1768-1774 begins after the Balta massacre (main article); Cliopatria drops about 164 cells in Ukraine and Moldova for 1769-1774.
November 1772: the Kaffa Eyalet leaves the Ottomans.
1774: the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca ends the war and grants Christians in Wallachia and Moldavia freedom of worship (main article).
1774: 'Ottoman Empire cedes Kerch, Enikale, Kabardia and part of Yedisan to Russia' at Küçük Kaynarca.
1774: Küçük Kaynarca granted the Crimean Khanate formal independence (the table calls it a Russian client state); in 1783 Russia 'annexed the Crimean Khanate.'
1787: the Russo-Turkish War of 1787-1792 begins.
1792: the Treaty of Jassy ends the war; the Ottomans recognise the annexation of the Crimean Khanate.
1792: 'Russia annexes Ozi' at Jassy and 'the Dniester was made the frontier in Europe.'
1798: Napoleon conquers Egypt.
1803: Egypt returns to the Ottoman shape.
1803: the Saudis take the Hejaz; the Muhammad Ali page says only that 'a second attack was launched in 1812 that succeeded in recapturing Hejaz,' so the first loss predates it.
1805: Cliopatria drops about 904 cells in Saudi Arabia and 29 in Jordan; no page dates the Saudi conquest of Medina.
1805: 'in 1805 he was named Wāli (governor) of Egypt.'
1805: the Serbian revolution ('1804-1815: Serbian revolution begins Balkan national awakening') removes Serbia from the Ottoman shape; the page gives only the span.
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: 1806: the Russo-Turkish War of 1806-1812 begins; Cliopatria drops about 71 cells of Ukraine, Moldova and Romania from 1807.

1811: 'In 1811, Muhammad Ali's Ottoman troops landed in Yanbu under the command of his son Tusun Pasha' (Wahhabi War); the fighting of 1812-1814 is in the Hejaz (Al-Safra, Medina in late 1812, Jeddah a month later, Mecca in January 1813, Taif in 1814).
1812: Muhammad Ali retakes the Hejaz.
1812: the Treaty of Bucharest ends the war of 1806-1812.
1812: 'Russia annexes Bessarabia' (Treaty of Bucharest; the text says Russia gained Bessarabia after the 1811 campaign).
1814: Serbia is back in the Ottoman shape; the page gives only the span of the revolution (1804-1815).
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: 1815: Serbia leaves again ('1804-1815: Serbian revolution'), this time for good.
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: Spring 1815: 'In the spring of 1815, Ottoman forces inflicted large-scale defeat upon the Saudis, forcing them to conclude a peace treaty'; 'the Wahhabis had to give up Hijaz'.

1816: 'the Ottomans resumed the war in 1816' and Ibrahim Pasha led the advance into Central Arabia; by 1817 'the armies had overrun Rass, Buraida and Unayza' and the siege of Diriyah ran from April to September 1818 (Wahhabi War).
1818: 'The Emirate of Diriyah is destroyed in 1818.'
1818: Ibrahim Pasha destroys Diriyah and Najd comes under the Ottomans' agent Muhammad Ali.
1821: 'Greece declares war on the Sultan' (the Greek War of Independence).
ledger.cpn: Greece (First Hellenic Republic, Kingdom of Greece, Second Hellenic Republic)

ledger.x: 1824: Najd leaves the Ottoman shape, the year the Second Saudi State begins; no page opened dates it.
June 1828: the Russians take ground.
1829: 'The Peloponnese and northern Gulf of Corinth win independence.'
ledger.cpn: Greece (First Hellenic Republic, Kingdom of Greece, Second Hellenic Republic)

ledger.x: September 1829: the Treaty of Adrianople ends the war.

September 1829: the Treaty of Adrianople 'gave Russia most of the eastern shore of the Black Sea': 'Russia kept the ports of Anapa and Poti, the border forts of Atskhur, Akhalkalaki and Akhaltsikhe'; the infobox adds the Danube Delta and Sujuk-Qale (Novorossiysk).
1830: 'The London Protocol formally recognises Greek independence.'
ledger.cpn: Greece (First Hellenic Republic, Kingdom of Greece, Second Hellenic Republic)

ledger.x: 1830: French forces invade and take Algiers (Deylik of Algiers) in 21 days (the main article's chronology); France's Algeria follows.
1830: 'Serbia's suzerainty as a hereditary monarchy is acknowledged de jure' (main article); the principality is an Ottoman vassal until 1878.
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: 31 October 1831: 'the Egyptian invasion of Syria initiated the First Turko-Egyptian War.'
5 May 1833: the Convention of Kütahya ends the First Egyptian-Ottoman War.

5 May 1833: the Convention of Kütahya 'gives Muhammad Ali the governorships of Crete, Aleppo, Tripoli, Damascus, and Sidon, plus tax rights in Adana'; the Muhammad Ali page adds Ibrahim Pasha as 'Wāli of Syria' and the Hijaz as compensation.
May 1835: 'Ottoman Sultan Mahmud II sent in troops ostensibly to restore order, but instead deposed and exiled Ali II, marking the end of both the Karamanli dynasty and an independent Tripolitania'.
June 1839: Ibrahim 'defeated the Ottomans at Nezib on 24 June 1839' in the second war.
27 November 1840: Muhammad Ali 'agreed to the London Convention terms,' ending the Second Egyptian-Ottoman War.
27 November 1840: Muhammad Ali's rule over the Levant ends.

13 February 1841: 'New firmans were issued which confined the pasha's authority to Egypt, including the Sinai peninsula' and the Sudan; 'Various restrictions were laid upon Muhammad Ali, emphasizing his position as vassal' (barred a fleet, army capped at 18,000), and 'The government of the pashalik of Egypt was made…

1865: the relation recorded under the dynasty's slug ends where the dynasty's own dossier ends it; the vassalage itself goes on under the Khedivate, whose dossier opens it again in 1866 (khedivate-of-egypt/ledger/1…
1873: Cliopatria adds about 637 cells in Yemen; its Imamate of Yemen row ends 1872.
1873: Cliopatria adds about 491 cells in Saudi Arabia, 55 in Kuwait and 48 in Qatar.
1877: the Russo-Turkish War of 1877-1878, 'a Russian victory'.
4 June 1878: the Cyprus Convention gives Britain administrative control of Cyprus: 'On 4 June, before the Congress opened on 13 June'; the island stays de jure Ottoman.
13 July 1878: the Treaty of Berlin ends the war ('the Congress culminated in the Treaty of Berlin (13 July 1878)').
29 July 1878: Austria-Hungary occupies Bosnia and Herzegovina, which stays Ottoman.
13 July 1878: Bulgaria becomes 'a semi-independent principality inside the Ottoman Empire,' with less than half the land planned at San Stefano.
13 July 1878: Eastern Rumelia becomes 'an autonomous province under a Christian ruler,' with Philippopolis (Plovdiv) as capital, under Ottoman control.
13 July 1878: Montenegro receives full independence and gains Nikšić, Podgorica, Bar and Plav-Gusinje.
13 July 1878: Serbia 'received full independence and lost territory'.
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: 13 July 1878: Romania receives full independence; Wallachia and Moldavia cease to be Ottoman vassals.
13 July 1878: Romania receives full independence; Moldavia ceases to be an Ottoman vassal.
13 July 1878: Romania 'gained Northern Dobruja'; it 'gave up Southern Bessarabia to Russia.'
ledger.cpn: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia (Principality and Kingdom of Romania to 1918)

ledger.x: 1878: 'Russia also received Kars and Ardahan' (the table: 'Kars Oblast and Batum Oblast were ceded to Russia').
1881: 'In 1881, after protracted negotiations, a compromise border' gives Thessaly and the Arta Prefecture to Greece under the Convention of Constantinople.
ledger.cpn: Greece (First Hellenic Republic, Kingdom of Greece, Second Hellenic Republic)

ledger.x: 12 May 1881: the French protectorate ends the beylik's tie to the Porte.
1885: Eastern Rumelia leaves the Ottoman shape; the Congress of Berlin page does not cover its union with Bulgaria.
1900: Kuwait leaves the Ottoman shape; the main article does not mention it.
1900: Crete leaves the Ottoman shape; Cliopatria has a Cretan State row for 1898-1899.
1908: Bulgaria declares its independence.
5 October 1908: the occupation becomes annexation.
5 October 1908: Austria-Hungary annexes Bosnia and Herzegovina.
1911-1912: 'Italo-Turkish War; the empire loses its North African territories and the Dodecanese.'
8 October 1912: 'The First Balkan War began on 8 October 1912, when the League member states attacked the Ottoman Empire' (Bulgaria, Serbia, Greece and Montenegro).
8 October 1912: Greece joins the Balkan League's attack.
ledger.cpn: Greece (First Hellenic Republic, Kingdom of Greece, Second Hellenic Republic)

ledger.x: 8 October 1912: Serbia joins the Balkan League's attack.
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: 1913: Cliopatria drops about 438 cells (Saudi Arabia 317, Qatar 48, Kuwait 37).
30 May 1913: the Treaty of London ends the war: 'all European territory of the Ottoman Empire west of the' Enos-Midiya line (Enez-Kıyıköy) is ceded to the Balkan League.
30 May 1913: the Treaty of London ends the war with Greece.
ledger.cpn: Greece (First Hellenic Republic, Kingdom of Greece, Second Hellenic Republic)

ledger.x: 30 May 1913: the Treaty of London ends the war with Serbia; the League's division of the land was left open and led to the Second Balkan War (16 June 1913).
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: 30 May 1913: 'Every Aegean island belonging to the Ottoman Empire, with the exception of Imbros and Tenedos,' goes to Greece, which also gains southern Epirus, southern Macedonia and Kavala (Treaty of Bucharest, 10 August 1913).
ledger.cpn: Greece (First Hellenic Republic, Kingdom of Greece, Second Hellenic Republic)

ledger.x: 1913: 'Macedonia was divided among the Balkan states'; Serbia gained northeastern Macedonia and the eastern half of the Sanjak of Novi Pazar at Bucharest (10 August 1913) and Montenegro the western half.
ledger.cpn: Serbia (Revolutionary Serbia, Principality and Kingdom of Serbia)

ledger.x: 1913: Bulgaria kept 'part of Macedonia (including Strumnitza) and western Thrace with its Aegean coastline, including Alexandroupolis' at Bucharest.
10 August 1913: the Treaty of Bucharest 'established the independent state of Albania' (Albania became independent under Great Power sponsorship).

30 September 1913: the Treaty of Constantinople returns Adrianople: 'Lozengrad, Lyule Burgas-Buni Hisar, and Adrianople reverted to the Ottomans' after the Ottomans won back Thrace in the Second Balkan War.
2 November 1914: Russia declares war on the Ottomans; 'Battle of Sarıkamış; Russian forces advance into northeastern Anatolia' (1914-1915).
1916: 'the Russian army captured Western Armenia in 1916.'
10 June 1916: the Arab Revolt begins at Mecca; it 'expels the Ottomans from much of the Hejaz and Transjordan, and takes Damascus.'
1917: 'Russia withdraws from Anatolia under the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk' (main article); the Russian pages give 1918 for the return to the pre-war borders.
1917: Allenby's British forces defeated the Ottomans 'in 1917 in the Sinai and Palestine campaign' and occupied Palestine and Syria.
1917: the Partition page gives no date for Baghdad; at San Remo in 1920 'Britain also received Mesopotamia and Iraq.'
1918: the Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen 'became independent in 1918'; the Treaty of Sèvres acknowledged it.
1918: the Ottomans recover the north-east.
October 1918: Syria passes out of Ottoman hands.
1919-1921: 'French forces occupied Cilicia during the Franco-Turkish War (1919-1921) and later left'.
1919: Cliopatria drops about 125 cells in Saudi Arabia; the Partition page does not mention Asir.
19 April 1919: the British 'occupied Kars on 19 April 1919' and placed the province under Armenian rule.
May 1919: 'Greece takes control of the Smyrna (İzmir) area.'

wars.name: Byzantine–Ottoman wars
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Bursa 1326, Karesi 1345-6, Çimpe 1354, Adrianople 1362-3, Thessaloniki 1387 and 1430, Constantinople on 29 May 1453; the emperor is a vassal from 1371.

wars.name: Battle of Kosovo
wars.outcome: On 15 June 1389 both armies were 'largely destroyed'; the Serbian principalities became Ottoman vassals in the following years (Stefan Lazarević in 1390).

wars.name: Crusade of Nicopolis
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory; Vidin is annexed and 'Bulgaria ceased to exist'.

wars.name: Ottoman Interregnum
wars.outcome: After Timur's victory at Ankara (1402) the beyliks regained their lands and the sons of Bayezid fought until Mehmed I defeated Musa outside Sofia in 1413.

wars.name: Crusade of Varna
wars.outcome: Murad II won at Varna on 10 November 1444; a peace of 1448 gave the Ottomans Wallachia, Bulgaria and part of Albania.

wars.name: Fall of Constantinople
wars.outcome: Mehmed II took Constantinople on 29 May 1453 after a siege that began in April; the Byzantine Empire ended.

wars.name: First Ottoman–Venetian War
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Negroponte, Lemnos and Albania Veneta captured (the page gives no separate dates).

wars.name: Second Ottoman–Venetian War
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Venice's strongholds in the Morea captured.

wars.name: Ottoman–Mamluk War (1516–1517)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory at Marj Dabiq (24 August 1516) and Ridaniya (24 January 1517); the Mamluk Sultanate is annexed, Syria, Egypt and the Hejaz become provinces and the caliphate passes to the Ottomans.

wars.name: Ottoman–Safavid War (1532–1555)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Baghdad taken in 1535; the Peace of Amasya (1555) 'partitions the Caucasus; Western Armenia, western Kurdistan, and Western Georgia go to the Ottomans'.

wars.name: Third Ottoman–Venetian War
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory; Venice surrenders most of its Aegean and Morea possessions in 1540.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of Hungary
wars.outcome: Mohács (1526) puts about a third of central Hungary under tribute; Buda falls in 1541 and the Ottomans hold the central and southern counties, the Habsburgs the west and north, Transylvania the east; in 1547 Ferdinand recognises Ottoman ascendancy.

wars.name: Ottoman–Venetian War (1570–1573)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Nicosia besieged 22 July 1570, Famagusta falls in August 1571; the fleet is beaten at Lepanto (1571) and peace is made in 1573.

wars.name: Ottoman–Safavid War (1578–1590)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: the Treaty of Constantinople (1590).

wars.name: Long Turkish War
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Zsitvatorok (1606) ended it; the war 'did not yield significant territorial changes'.

wars.name: Ottoman–Safavid War (1603–1618)
wars.outcome: Persian victory: the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha (1612) ceded the Caucasus, except westernmost Georgia; the Treaty of Serav (1618) confirmed it.

wars.name: Ottoman–Safavid War (1623–1639)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Baghdad lost on 14 January 1624, retaken in December 1638; the Treaty of Zuhab (17 May 1639) leaves the Ottomans Baghdad and all Mesopotamia, western Georgia, Western Armenia and Samtskhe, and the Safavids Eastern Armenia (Revan), Dagestan…

wars.name: Cretan War (1645–1669)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Crete conquered ('completed' in 1669); Venice loses Dalmatia, Aegean islands and Crete.

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1663–1664)
wars.outcome: The Ottomans conquered Nové Zámky (Uyvar) in 1663; the war ended at the Battle of St.

wars.name: Great Turkish War
wars.outcome: Habsburg-led Holy League victory: Buda reconquered in 1686, the Morea taken by Venice, and the Treaty of Karlowitz (26 January 1699) gives the Austrians the rest of Hungary and overlordship of Transylvania; Podolia returns to Poland.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1676–1681)
wars.outcome: Disputed; the Treaty of Bakhchisarai 'established the Russo-Turkish border on the Dnieper River'.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1686–1700)
wars.outcome: Russian victory: the Treaty of Constantinople (1700) gives Russia Azov, Taganrog, Pavlovsk and Mius.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1710–1711)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory on the Pruth: Russia returned Azov (treaties of Pruth and Adrianople, 1713).

wars.name: Ottoman–Venetian War (1714–1718)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: the Morea, Tinos and Aigina recaptured, 'the last Venetian holdings in the Aegean'.

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1716–1718)
wars.outcome: Habsburg victory: Prince Eugene wins at Petrovaradin (1716) and takes Belgrade (1717); Passarowitz (1718) gives the Austrians the Banat of Temeswar, Serbia and Oltenia.

wars.name: Ottoman–Persian War (1730–1735)
wars.outcome: Persian victory; Treaty of Constantinople (1736).

wars.name: Austro-Russian–Turkish War (1735–1739)
wars.outcome: Ottoman gains from Austria: the Treaty of Belgrade (1739) returns Serbia with Belgrade, the southern Banat and northern Bosnia, with the Sava and Danube as the line; Oltenia goes to Wallachia.

wars.name: Ottoman–Persian War (1743–1746)
wars.outcome: Indecisive; Treaty of Kerden (1746).

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1768–1774)
wars.outcome: Russian victory: Küçük Kaynarca cedes Kerch, Enikale, Kabardia and part of Yedisan; the Crimean Khanate becomes formally independent.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1787–1792)
wars.outcome: Russian victory: Jassy (1792) gives Russia Ozi (Ochakov) and the Dniester frontier; Austria's Sistova gains (1791) were 'meager' (Orșova and two small towns).

wars.name: Serbian Revolution
wars.outcome: Serbia wins autonomy; its 'suzerainty as a hereditary monarchy' is acknowledged de jure in 1830.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1806–1812)
wars.outcome: Russian victory: Bucharest (1812) gives Russia Bessarabia.

wars.name: Ottoman–Saudi War (1811–1818)
wars.outcome: Muhammad Ali retakes the Hejaz in 1812 and destroys the Emirate of Diriyah in 1818.

wars.name: Greek War of Independence
wars.outcome: Greek victory: independence for the Peloponnese and the northern Gulf of Corinth in 1829, recognised by the London Protocol of 1830; the Egyptian fleet is lost at Navarino (20 October 1827).

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1828–1829)
wars.outcome: Russian victory: the Treaty of Adrianople; Russia occupies the Danubian principalities and receives the Black Sea coast of the Caucasus and western Georgia.

wars.name: Egyptian–Ottoman War (1831–1833)
wars.outcome: Egyptian victory at Konya (21 December 1832); the Convention of Kütahya (5 May 1833) gives Muhammad Ali the governorships of Crete, Aleppo, Tripoli, Damascus and Sidon.

wars.name: Egyptian–Ottoman War (1839–1841)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory with British and Austrian help: Muhammad Ali accepts the London Convention (27 November 1840), keeps Egypt and Sudan as hereditary rule and renounces Crete and the Hijaz.

wars.name: Crimean War
wars.outcome: Allied and Ottoman victory: by the Treaty of Paris Russia cedes southern Bessarabia and recognises de jure Ottoman suzerainty over the Danubian principalities.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878)
wars.outcome: Russian victory: the Treaty of Berlin (13 July 1878) makes Bulgaria a vassal principality, gives full independence to Romania, Serbia and Montenegro, hands Kars, Ardahan and Batum to Russia, Bosnia to Austria-Hungary's administration and Cyprus to Britain.

wars.name: Italo-Turkish War
wars.outcome: Italian victory: the empire loses its North African territories and the Dodecanese.

wars.name: First Balkan War
wars.outcome: Balkan League victory: by the Treaty of London (30 May 1913) the Ottomans lose all European land west of the Enos-Midiya line and every Aegean island but Imbros and Tenedos; Albania becomes independent.

wars.name: Second Balkan War
wars.outcome: The Ottomans win back Adrianople; the Treaty of Constantinople (30 September 1913) returns Lozengrad, Lyule Burgas-Buni Hisar and Adrianople.

wars.name: Middle Eastern theatre of World War I
wars.outcome: Ottoman defeat: the Armistice of Mudros (30 October 1918) opens the partition; Russia captured Western Armenia in 1916 and withdrew in 1917, the British took Baghdad and Palestine in 1917 and Syria in 1918.

wars.name: Arab Revolt
wars.outcome: The revolt begins at Mecca on 10 June 1916 and expels the Ottomans from much of the Hejaz and Transjordan and takes Damascus; Hussein bin Ali founds the Kingdom of Hejaz.

wars.name: Turkish War of Independence
wars.outcome: Turkish National Movement victory: the Treaty of Sèvres (1920) is superseded at Lausanne (1923); the sultanate is abolished on 1 November 1922.

certainty.note: Beylik, march and Anatolian-interior frontiers are approximate.

The European frontiers follow treaties (Karlowitz 1699, Passarowitz 1718, Belgrade 1739, Küçük Kaynarca 1774, Jassy 1792, Bucharest 1812, Adrianople 1829, Paris 1856, Berlin 1878, London 1913) and the Russian frontier follows them to 1878.
Wartime fronts, the Allied occupation zones and the 1919-1922 Anatolian fronts move monthly; the drawn shape is Cliopatria's yearly outline.
